author: Vieillot, 1819
habitat: 온화한 내륙 물가, 얕은 민물 늪, 호수, 연못, 염분 있는 호수
summary: 몸이 가늘고 다리가 긴 중소형 도요새이다. 대초원 같은 탁 트인 곳의 얕은 민물 늪이나 온화한 내륙 물가에서 번식하고, 호수나 연못에서 겨울을 난다. 이동할 때나 겨울에는 소금기 있거나 알칼리성인 호수에 모인다. 미시간, 온타리오 서부, 미네소타, 캘리포니아 동부, 오리건 중부, 워싱턴, 브리티시컬럼비아, 콜로라도 남부, 애리조나 중부 등지에서 번식하고, 아마존강 부근을 뺀 남아메리카와 아르헨티나 등에서 겨울을 난다.

sexes.male: 정수리가 어둡고 윗면은 회갈색이며, 윗가슴에 밤색 기가 조금 돌고 아랫면은 흰색이다.

art.subject: Wilson's Phalarope (Phalaropus tricolor), adult female in breeding plumage, as seen in spring: crown and hindneck pale silvery grey; a black stripe from the bill base through the eye and down the side of the neck, turning deep wine-chestnut on the lower neck; white throat, with a warm orange-buff wash on the foreneck; back and scapulars grey with two long wine-chestnut stripes; wings grey-brown; underparts white; rump white. Long, needle-thin black bill; dark eye; black legs.
art.pose: wading in shallow fresh water, side view
art.scene: Korean shallow freshwater marsh beside an open lake in May; no people, buildings or text
views: adult female breeding, side view standing in shallow water: needle-thin black bill, pale grey crown, black stripe through the eye turning wine-chestnut down the neck side, grey back with chestnut stripes, white underparts, long black legs
adult male breeding, side view standing: duller and browner than the female, darker crown, grey-brown upperparts, faint chestnut on the neck and upper breast, white underparts, black legs
art.build: Slender, long-necked wader, a little larger than the Red-necked Phalarope and close to the Marsh Sandpiper in size, with a small head. Bill black, straight and needle-thin, slightly longer than the head. Legs long, black in the breeding season and yellow in winter; toes narrowly lobed. Wings plain, with no wing bar; in flight plain grey-brown wings and a white rump. Feeds by walking briskly on mud and spinning on shallow water. Males are duller than females.
avoid: Do not add a white wing bar; Red-necked and Red Phalaropes have one, Wilson's does not.
Do not paint a red patch on the neck with a dark grey head (female Red-necked Phalarope, Phalaropus lobatus).
Do not make the bill thick or curved; it is straight and needle-thin.
